correctness.rationale: Exponent pattern (2,1,1) forces odd exclusion using σ(n)/n≤(13/9)(6/5)(8/7)<2, and even shapes 4pq, 2p²q, 2pq² with p<q odd. Upper σ(n)/n<3 ensures omissions proper. For 4pq, Δ=56−(p−7)(q−7) and three-divisor coefficient comparison gives 32 possible prime pairs. For 2p²q, Δ=(3+3p−p²)q+3(p²+p+1), leaving 12; for 2pq², Δ=(3−p)q²+3(p+1)(q+1), leaving 4. These global inequalities reduce the infinite theorem to exactly 48 candidates. Independent newly written exact integer enumeration over each candidate’s complete 12-divisor set and all 165 proper triples reproduces 25 integers, 32 unordered witnesses, and 17/6/2 solutions by shape. This is finite exhaustiveness after analytical bounds, not a search horizon.
